rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> laboratory soil-column experiment with repacked Brown Forest and Lou soils at several bulk densities, subsurface drip irrigation (350 mL) and aeration (1050 mL) through the emitter, air permeability measured with a transient flow apparatus. Q2: Results, 'Impact of Aeration following Drip Irrigation', Fig. 6a<U+2013>6f <U+2013> aeration through the subsurface drip emitter after irrigation raised air permeability within 10 min to 3.7, 2.0 and 1.5 times the pre-aeration level (Brown Forest soil, bulk density 1.3/1.4/1.5) and 3.0, 2.5, 2.0 times (Lou soil), reaching ~70% and ~88% of pre-irrigation levels versus 54.8% and 67.6% at 24 h without aeration. Q8: Results and Conclusions <U+2013> authors note disturbed repacked samples were used so soil structure may have been destroyed (offered to explain contradiction with Schj<U+00F8>nning et al. 1999), and state that further experiments with undisturbed structured soils are needed.
rows.notes: Single lab method (transient flow apparatus) only, no second independent method. Mechanism (air forcing water redistribution, increasing pore continuity) is asserted ('probably') rather than measured; soil water content was not directly measured. Only two soils and three bulk densities, lab columns, no field/farm scale. Effect varied with texture and bulk density but no condition stated as a requirement. Single columns per treatment; no SD, CI or range reported for the aeration effect (only R2 of regression fits).

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a laboratory column experiment on air permeability under subsurface drip irrigation with and without post-irrigation aeration through the emitter; no crop, field or soil strength/air-filled porosity measurements.
